items.title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
items.summary_1line: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: t...
items.editor_note: Frames the multi-agent design problem: delegation saves main-agent context but fails without coordinated task allocation.

items.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
items.summary_1line: DRBench Pro is a benchmark that scores deep research agents by how broadly and deeply their reports cover knowledge from Wikipedia-derived trees, with 144 cases, 44,102 rubrics, and a best agent at 57.04% coverage.
items.editor_note: Adds a coverage benchmark with a hard number: the best agent covers 57.04% of rubric knowledge.

items.title: Show HN: Shandu 4.0 – Local sleek deep research agent that audits every citation
items.summary_1line: Shandu is an open-source local deep research agent with a CLI and web UI that searches the web, arXiv, PubMed and PDFs, and audits every cited sentence against its source text, using any LiteLLM-supported model.
items.editor_note: First practitioner tool in the thread: runs locally and verifies citations sentence by sentence.

editorial.tldr: This is a research-theme thread, not one event: through October and early November, papers reworked deep research agents around iterative state, video sources and page-image input. On Nov 12 and Nov 25 the focus moved to multi-agent coordination and to scoring report coverage.
editorial.whats_new: On Nov 27, Shandu 4.0 shipped as an open-source local deep research agent that checks every cited sentence against its source text, with any LiteLLM-supported model.
editorial.why_it_matters: Deep research is moving from demos to measurable systems: coordination cost, rubric-scored coverage and per-sentence citation checks are now concrete things to evaluate in your own research agent.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you ship a research agent, add a per-sentence citation check against retrieved source text before release, and score report coverage with rubrics instead of judging fluency.

status.detail: Loosely linked work on how deep research agents split work, get scored and prove their citations.

open_questions: Does Shandu's citation audit catch unsupported claims that DRBench Pro-style coverage rubrics miss?
Will any multi-agent deep research system report a DRBench Pro score above 57.04%?
What token or latency overhead does coordinated multi-agent delegation add over a single agent?
Do page-image (vision-language) inputs from earlier work raise coverage on benchmarks like DRBench Pro?
